sources.entry: TypeScript: _Tiny Package Manager: Learns how npm or Yarn works_

summary.one_liner: A small educational TypeScript demo that implements a simplified package manager to show how npm or Yarn work under the hood.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a tiny package manager meant as a guide rather than a replacement for npm or Yarn. It downloads packages into a node_modules directory and provides a simple CLI. It resolves dependency conflicts in a simplified way and flattens the dependency tree. It supports a lock file similar to yarn.lock or package-lock.json. It can add a new package through the CLI, like yarn add or npm i. The README says the code in the src directory is commented to explain how it works, starting from src/index.ts. Lifecycle scripts (preinstall/postinstall) and bin symlinking are listed as not yet implemented.
use_cases: learn how npm or Yarn resolve dependencies
read a commented example of lock file handling
how_to_run: cd into a directory containing a valid package.json
notable: Designed as a readable, commented learning guide to package manager internals
Flattens the dependency tree and resolves conflicts in a simplified way
Supports a lock file and adding packages via CLI
caveats: Intentionally skips many edge cases and error handling
Lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall) are not implemented
Not intended as a production replacement for npm or Yarn
